title: private-deploy-networking-debug-notes
content:
Debugging notes - Private deploy networking issues (scratchpad)

Context:
- Customer private deployment (VPC peering + private endpoints) failing to reach Redwood control-plane endpoints from customer subnet. Impact: control plane heartbeats / agent checkins intermittently fail.
- Customer environment: AWS account, VPC peering to Redwood-managed VPC. Route tables, security groups partially reviewed by infra SME (Aisha).
- Repro environment: replicate with a test EC2 in customer subnet + agent container.

Observed symptoms (high level):
- Agent frequently loses connection to control-plane (every ~5-20m). When it fails, agent logs show TLS handshake errors or connection timeouts.
- Some pods/instances can reach control-plane for hours, others never. Flaky across AZs.
- DNS sometimes resolves control-plane host to private IP in Redwood VPC, sometimes to public IP (unexpected).

Timeline / quick log:
- 2024-11-06 09:15: first report from CS: agent not checking in.
- 2024-11-06 10:02: I (Eliot) ran initial dig/nslookup from customer EC2.
- 2024-11-07 14:30: Confirmed VPC peering status Active, but missing route in customer-route-table for /16 of Redwood VPC (patched temporarily).
- 2024-11-08 11:05: TLS handshake error observed after route fix.
- 2024-11-09 08:43: Found iptables egress rule blocking ephemeral ports on one bastion host (mitigated).

Commands tried (notes + outputs paraphrased):
- dig control.prod.redwood-inference.internal @10.0.0.2 +short
  -> 10.200.4.12
- nslookup control.prod.redwood-inference.internal
  -> Server: 10.0.0.2
     Address: 10.0.0.2#53
     Name: control.prod.redwood-inference.internal
     Address: 10.200.4.12
- curl -v https://control.prod.redwood-inference.internal:443/health --connect-timeout 10
  -> * Connected to control.prod.redwood-inference.internal (10.200.4.12) port 443 (#0)
     * TLSv1.3 (IN HANDSHAKE)
     * error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca
     * Closing connection 0
     curl: (35) error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca
- openssl s_client -connect 10.200.4.12:443 -servername control.prod.redwood-inference.internal -showcerts
  -> CONNECTED(00000003)
     depth=2 C = US, O = Redwood Inference, CN = Redwood Root CA
     verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
     ---
     ??? certificate chain truncated / not presenting full chain on some servers
- traceroute -n 10.200.4.12
  -> 1  10.0.1.1 (customer-igw)
     2  10.0.5.254 (customer-vpn)
     3  100.64.1.17 (transit)
     *  *  * (sometimes stops at transit device)
- aws ec2 describe-vpc-peering-connections --filters Name=status-code,Values=active
  -> shows peering-abc123 Active between vpc-1111 (customer) and vpc-2222 (redwood)
- aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-1111
  -> missing route for 10.200.0.0/16 in one private RT (AZ-specific).
- sudo iptables -L -n | grep DROP
  -> found rule: -A OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 32768:60999 -j DROP  (this was on a bastion host; ephemeral ports blocked)
- kubectl exec -it agent-pod -- curl -v https://control.prod.redwood-inference.internal:443/health
  -> Pod DNS resolves to 10.200.4.12 but connect times out (no immediate TLS error)

Intermittent behaviors noticed:
- DNS resolution alternates between private IP (10.200.4.12) and public IP (34.210.112.9). When it resolves to public IP, traffic must egress to internet and then back to Redwood; customer's NACLs block that path in private subnets -> connection fails.
- Some Redwood control-plane hosts are misconfigured and present incomplete certificate chains (missing intermediate cert). When agent hits those hosts -> openssl verify fails with "unable to get local issuer certificate" and curl returns unknown ca. Other hosts present full chain and work. Implies inconsistent cert deployment across control-plane fleet.

Hypotheses / root-cause candidates:
1) Route table asymmetry: not all private route tables had peering/routing for Redwood VPC CIDR. Causes some AZs to try egress-to-internet fallback (DNS split-horizon) -> intermittent failures. Evidence: missing route in one RT.
2) DNS split-horizon / resolver caching: customer resolver sometimes returns public IPs for control host (likely because conditional forwarder to Redwood DNS is inconsistent or TTL caching across resolvers).
3) Partial cert rollout / misconfiguration on Redwood control-plane: some hosts missing intermediate certs (causing unknown CA errors). Need ops cert rollout check.
4) Egress / iptables / NACL blocking ephemeral ports on certain host(s) causing TLS handshake to stall (SYN succeeds but ephemeral ports blocked prevents response).
5) MTU / fragmentation between networks (less likely but keep as low-priority).

Immediate mitigations applied so far:
- Added missing route to the customer private route table for Redwood VPC CIDR (10.200.0.0/16) — reduced number of failures.
- Removed the iptables DROP rule on a bastion used for testing (Aisha to confirm across fleet).
- Added short-term DNS TTL reduction on control host records (to 30s) while we debug resolver behavior.

Next steps (actionable):
- [ ] Ops: run cert-check across control-plane endpoints (script to curl --cacert RedwoodRoot.pem and check chain). Find hosts missing intermediate certs and force re-deploy (Assign to Ops: Samir). Linked: github PR with cert rollout? (see linked_artifacts).
- [ ] Net: audit all customer route tables across AZs for peering route presence (10.200.0.0/16) and ensure propagated where needed (Eliot + Aisha).
- [ ] DNS: check conditional forwarders / resolvers on customer side. Identify why some resolvers return public IPs. Temporary: enforce response policy to prefer private answers. (Maya asked to run 'dig +trace' from multiple subnets).
- [ ] Security: scan for iptables rules/NACLs that drop ephemeral ports or outbound 443. Provide list of affected hosts. (Aisha).
- [ ] Add more verbose agent logs around TLS handshake to capture server cert bytes for failing connections (instrumentation ticket INFRA-3421).
- [ ] Add passive monitoring to detect certificate chain issues (metric: TLS_verify_fail_count per host).

Notes to self / heuristics learned:
- When seeing intermittent control-plane connectivity in private-deploys, check in this order: route-tables (peering) -> DNS (split-horizon / resolvers) -> per-host iptables/NACL -> cert chain consistency -> MTU. This order matches common faults we see.
- Short TTL trick helps observe resolver behavior quickly (but be careful, may spike queries).
- For customer reproducibility, always test from multiple subnets/AZs and from a pod/container to catch differences in VPC routing vs bastion host behavior.

Quick commands to reproduce checklist (for on-call):
- dig @<customer-resolver> control.prod.redwood-inference.internal +short; repeat from multiple subnets
- curl -v --resolve control.prod.redwood-inference.internal:443:<private-ip> https://control.prod.redwood-inference.internal/health --cacert RedwoodRoot.pem
- openssl s_client -connect <private-ip>:443 -servername control.prod.redwood-inference.internal -showcerts | sed -n '1,120p'
- aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=<customer-vpc> | grep -E '10.200' -C 3
- sudo iptables -L -n; check for DROP on OUTPUT or FORWARD chains

Unresolved questions / TODO:
- Why are some control-plane hosts returning public IPs in DNS? Is there an authoritative DNS server misconfigured or missing conditional forwarding for some zones?
- Confirm cert issuance flow: are we mixing certs from two CAs? Does the intermediate CA change per region? (Possible if auto-rolling with expired intermediate).
- Does the AWS Transit/partner path occasionally NAT traffic causing unexpected source IPs -> firewall rules deny? (Check transit logs).

If anything new appears I'll paste raw logs here. Keep this doc as single-source scratchpad until we have a postmortem.

-- Eliot
